extracted.intended_audience: readers of film criticism / general moviegoing public
extracted.subtask_description: Critically evaluating a contemporary teen sex-comedy film with attention to character work, thematic ambition (sexuality, patriarchy, sex work), comedic execution, and cultural plausibility. The review judges how well the film's ideas and jokes are developed and positioned within the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of social commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the film's attempt to 'flip the script' or comment on female sexuality, patriarchal exploitation, and sex-work stigma actually land? The review faults Summer Of 69 for commentary that 'flops' and is 'superficial at best, glaringly lazy at worst.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for substantive, nuanced insight rather than surface-level statements; avoid token gestures that don't interrogate power dynamics. A successful film will unpack contradictions instead of skimming them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of character development and interiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the protagonists and supporting figures fleshed out with believable backstories, interior lives, and motivations? The reviewer criticizes Abby and Santa Monica for lacking revealed backgrounds and interiorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should have coherent motivations and personal histories that inform their actions and choices; avoid using characters merely as props for plot or jokes. Emotional arcs should be earned and explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic nuance and willingness to critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the film interrogate the tensions it raises (e.g., between sexual empowerment and exploitation) or does it adopt an uncritical stance? The review argues the film's sex-positivity is 'so forgiving that there is no room for critique.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good work acknowledges complexity and examines trade-offs rather than presenting a single, unexamined solution (e.g., 'girlbossing' as a cure-all).

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of sex work and its structural implications
rubrics_metrics.description: How honestly and responsibly does the film portray strip clubs, sex workers' agency, shame, and economic constraints? The review notes Santa Monica is objectified by men, ashamed, and focused on buying the club, yet the film fails to address what her ownership would mean for other women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the film grapples with systemic issues (safety, exploitation, labor conditions) and the consequences of proposed solutions, rather than reducing sex work to personal morality tales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of female sexual agency versus male pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the narrative decouple women's sexual self-discovery from prioritizing male gratification? The reviewer argues the film views women's sexual discovery as hinging on partner gratification and doesn't show how to divorce sexual identity from male pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether female desire is depicted on its own terms (including masturbation, consent, boundaries) and whether plots reproduce the trope that women's sexual value is validated by male satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic writing and joke execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the jokes, comic set pieces, and overall comedic tone sharp, original, and well-paced? The reviewer says the film 'doesn’t flesh out its ... jokes with enough finesse' to belong in the teen sex comedy canon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor should be specific, earned from character and situation, and balanced with tonal control—avoid relying on cheap gags or provocative concepts without payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-savviness and standing within the canon
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the film meaningfully contribute to or rank within the established teen sex-comedy canon? The review finds it fails to 'rank within the storied teen sex comedy canon.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the film's originality, thematic ambition, and comic craftsmanship to genre exemplars; mere novelty of premise isn't sufficient to claim a place in the canon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausibility and cultural/contextual accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Are character decisions and plot choices credible within the contemporary cultural context (e.g., why a teen would hire an in-person stripper instead of finding sex-advice online)? The reviewer flags Abby's decision as 'oddly retro' given modern social media/OnlyFans culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the film acknowledges present-day norms and technologies or needs to justify retro choices plausibly; small disbeliefs can undermine the story if unexplained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal plot logic and transactional stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Do monetary amounts, motivations, and transactional exchanges make sense and drive believable stakes (e.g., Abby's payments to Santa Monica and Santa Monica's need to buy the club)? The review notes the $5,000/$20,000 arrangement and its connection to Santa Monica's goal to buy the club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot transactions should have clear, believable consequences and motivate character choices; coincidences or convenient sums should be scrutinized for plausibility and dramatic weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional authenticity of relationships and camaraderie
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the evolving bond between characters (here, Abby and Santa Monica) rendered authentically with real give-and-take, or is it superficially sketched? The review says their bond 'slowly develops' but more isn't revealed about their backgrounds and interiorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relationships should transform characters and reveal vulnerabilities; warmth or camaraderie must be grounded in specific shared experiences or revelations to feel earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with socio-religious context (erotic repression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the film explore relevant cultural factors—like Catholic upbringing and erotic repression—that shape characters' sexualities? The reviewer says there's 'no investigation of the erotic repression the religion is notorious for.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a film invokes a cultural or religious backdrop, it should meaningfully incorporate how those institutions influence character psychology and choices, rather than using them as superficial markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sex-positive moments and narrative integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Are sex-positive scenes (e.g., masturbation-empowerment sequences or conversations about readiness) integrated into the story in a way that furthers character growth and thematic complexity? The reviewer acknowledges a sex-store sequence emphasizing masturbation but says the script offers little broader insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolated empowering beats must be tied into characters' arcs and the film's thematic argument; otherwise they register as token or performative.
